sources.name: OGC API - Processes - Part 1: Core 1.0
sources.role: process description, execution mode, job-state and output contract
verified_facts: A process description declares its inputs and outputs before execution.
Execution may be synchronous or asynchronous; asynchronous execution exposes a job resource whose status and result links describe processing lifecycle.
A successful job/result indicates process completion, not independent validation of the source data used by that process.
semantic_limits: A completed process is not authoritative terrain or parcel-height evidence by itself.
Outputs remain fail-closed unless source asset identity, digest, CRS, units and parameter lineage are bound.
Job status and retry state must never create a business row.

sources.name: OGC SensorThings API Part 1: Sensing 1.1
sources.role: observation time, datastream, unit and feature-of-interest contract
verified_facts: An Observation carries a result and phenomenonTime and is linked to a Datastream and FeatureOfInterest.
resultTime is distinct from phenomenonTime and records when the result became available.
A Datastream binds observations to a Sensor, ObservedProperty, Thing and unitOfMeasurement.
semantic_limits: A numeric observation without its datastream, unit, time and feature-of-interest binding is not parcel-elevation evidence.
SensorThings conformance does not establish ODN height, DTM semantics or an authoritative vertical CRS.
Observation resultQuality metadata is not a substitute for primary-source validation.

sources.name: OGC API - Environmental Data Retrieval - Part 1: Core
sources.role: environmental parameter, query geometry, extent, CRS and subset contract
verified_facts: Collection metadata advertises available parameters, units, extents and supported query resources.
EDR query resources include spatial forms such as position, area, cube, trajectory and corridor when supported.
A response is a selected environmental-data subset whose parameter and coordinate context must remain bound.
semantic_limits: A successful position, area or cube query does not prove exact HMLR polygon containment.
Subsetting, interpolation or reprojection does not independently establish the source vertical datum or measurement accuracy.
An EDR response subset is not proof that the complete source raster was read.

sources.name: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.role: quality metric, measurement, annotation and provenance contract
verified_facts: A dqv:QualityMeasurement associates a value with a quality metric and the resource on which it was computed.
A dqv:QualityMetric describes the quality calculation being applied; quality annotations express assessments separately.
Quality metadata can be connected to provenance and dataset/catalog metadata without becoming the measured domain value.
semantic_limits: A quality score is metadata and must not be interpreted as an elevation measurement.
The 4/4 QA score must not be converted into parcel-height confidence or a business result.
Metric definition, computed resource and provenance are required before comparing quality measurements.
